items.text: Hong Kong will give 500,000 air tickets to lure tourists and businesses back to the city. On Thursday, a global publicity campaign launched called ‘Hello Hong Kong’; it launched with dancers and flashing neon lights in the city’s main convention center beside its famous harbor. The city’s leader John Lee announced the giveaway at the launch of the campaign, and he highlighted that a number of events will happen, including the Rugby Sevens and the city marathon. The government is seeking to revive the economy and repair Hong Kong’s global image after 2019’s violent protests and three years of self-imposed isolation during the pandemic. The giveaway will begin at the start of March and will last six months. People have different ways to win tickets, such as a lottery and two-for-one purchases. Hong Kong received around 605,000 visitors last year as the city slowly dropped its COVID-19 restrictions, compared to almost 56 million before the pandemic in 2019. Difficult words: lure (to tempt a person or animal to do something by offering a reward), revive (to give new energy or strength), self-imposed (a task or situation that you have deliberately created or accepted for yourself). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2019, almost 56 million people visited Hong Kong. When the pandemic started, Hong Kong imposed very strict rules, and the country closed to visitors for three years. In 2019, many protests happened, which hurt the city’s reputation . In 2022, as a result, only 605,000 visitors came. Now, the city is ready to welcome tourists again, and the government has an interesting plan. Hong Kong will give away 500,000 air tickets to reward tourists and companies to return. People can win tickets in a lottery or buy two tickets for the price of one. The city’s leader started a campaign called ‘Hello Hong Kong’. Many events will happen, so officials hope they will bring visitors to the city. Some events are a city marathon and a rugby match. Difficult words: impose (to start something or to control), reputation (the feeling people have about something), marathon (a long exciting race). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2019, almost 56 million people visit Hong Kong. Then the Coronavirus starts. Hong Kong has very serious COVID rules. The city is in isolation for three years. Last year, only 605,000 visitors come to Hong Kong. This situation is bad for business. Hong Kong needs tourists and companies to come back. Officials say that the city will give away 500,000 air tickets. People can win the tickets. Or if they buy one ticket, they can get one for free . The city will also host many events. Some are a rugby match and a race. Difficult words: isolation (be separate from other people to stop a sickness), give away (to give something freely as a gift), for free (when you get something and you do not have to pay for it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China may ban the export of technology for solar panels. The country dominates the industry by controlling at least 75% of its global supply chain. This situation creates repercussions for the West’s hope to create its own green energy industry. In the “chip war” between the West and China, America is slowing China’s technological development. America restricts the exports of tools and software used to make advanced chips. Chinese media reported that the ban covers technology and machinery used to create solar panel parts such as large wafers , black silicon, and ultra-efficient silicon ingots . However, to protect the export market, the ban doesn’t apply to China’s solar panels themselves. Western companies have the experience and intellectual property used in the solar industry that developed in America and Europe. This industry occurred before low-cost China scaled up its production and had control. However, building new factories for solar parts would take a few years, and creating an entire solar supply chain could take four times as long. Difficult words: repercussion (an unwelcome consequence of an event or action), wafer (a thin slice of an electronic part), ingot (an unfinished piece of material, usually metal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese media reported that the country would ban the outside sale of solar panel components . China controls 75% of the world’s solar supply chain , and Western countries are not very happy about the situation. The United States and Europe would like to have their own solar energy industry, but they currently depend on components from China. China’s ban should cover photovoltaic technology but not China’s solar panels themselves. Before China controlled the market, Western countries had the right skills and knowledge for solar technology. If Western companies want to build factories for solar panel components, it will take them many years. Difficult words: component (a part of a machine or vehicle), supply chain (all the people and companies who make and deliver a product), photovoltaic technology (materials and devices which change sunlight into electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Solar energy comes from the sun. The photovoltaic business changes solar energy into electricity. China controls most of the business. The Chinese media say that China wants to stop the export of components for solar panels. This news is not good for Western countries. They need components from China. The country will still export solar panels. American and European engineers know how to make solar panels. The business hasn’t fully grown in the West. China has power. The United States and Europe have no factories to make solar components. People need many years to build the factories. Difficult words: export (to send things to another country for people to buy), component (a part of a machine or vehicle), West , Western (countries that are west of Asia, usually Europe, the UK, and the US). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hundreds of wildfires are burning across Chile, so the government extended an emergency order to another region on Saturday. Due to a scorching summer heatwave and high winds, authorities have struggled to contain the fires that have claimed at least 23 lives. Some rescue efforts ended in further tragedy when an emergency support helicopter crashed and killed two rescuers. A firefighter also died while trying to battle flames. More than 1,100 people have sought refuge in shelters, and the disaster has disrupted traffic on various highways. Authorities said that the adverse weather conditions would continue as temperatures soar above 38 degrees Celsius, and they predict more strong winds in the affected areas. Difficult words: scorching (very hot), refuge (a place or situation where a person is safe), adverse (harmful or unfavorable). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hundreds of wildfires are burning in Chile, and they already destroyed many homes and thousands of acres of forest. Last week, the Chilean government declared a state of emergency in several regions, and other regions may join soon. At least 23 people died already, including three rescuers, and hundreds were hurt. More than 1,100 people had to leave their homes to seek shelter . The fires also affected traffic on highways. Authorities said that it was very difficult to get the fires under control because of strong winds and high temperatures. They expected the conditions to continue with temperatures above 38 degrees Celsius. Difficult words: state of emergency (a danger or disaster when the government has power to control the situation), seek (to look for something), shelter (a place where a person is safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hundreds of wildfires are burning in Chile. They destroy hundreds of homes. They burn large areas of forest. The situation is very serious. Summer is happening in Chile. Temperatures are unusually high. They are above 38 degrees Celsius. Strong winds spread the fires. Firefighters cannot get the fires under control. 1,100 people must leave their homes. They are not safe. 23 people die. Three rescuers also die. A state of emergency is in some places in Chile. The state of emergency gives the government more power than normal. Authorities can control the situation better. The work is still very difficult. They say that hot weather will continue. Difficult words: wildfire (a large fire which spreads quickly from natural places to other places), destroy (to affect something so badly that people cannot use it anymore), spread (to move across a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rescue workers in the far east of Russia braved freezing waters to save four orcas, who were trapped between ice at 50–100 metres from the coastline. They were stuck overnight, with the head of the region’s emergency ministry explaining that the waters are shallow and filled with stones. The team of people took a small boat to reach the whales and moved the ice to create gaps that the whales could swim through. It took them several hours but three of the whales, including one calf, were freed. They stayed with the fourth orca, protecting it from the ice, until higher waters allowed it to join the others. Difficult words: brave (to get through a difficult experience), trapped (not be able to move), head (a leader), calf (a young animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ice trapped four orcas in the far east of Russia. Rescue workers took a small boat to reach the whales that were between 50 to 100 metres from the coastline. They then had to move the ice to create gaps the whales could swim through. It took a few hours, but they managed to get three of the whales, including one calf , to freedom. The rescuers stayed with the fourth orca, protecting it from the ice, until higher waters allowed it to join the others. Difficult words: orca (a big, black and white toothed whale), trapped (not able to move), calf (a young animal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Four orcas are in the far east of Russia. They get trapped between ice. People help them. They take a small boat and go to the orcas. People move the ice. They make space for the orcas. This takes hours. Three orcas get free. One of them is young. The fourth orca is still trapped. People wait for higher waters. When there’s more water, the orca joins the others. Difficult words: orca (a big, black and white toothed whale), trapped (not able to move), join (to get to the others, to become part of the group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Anglo-Australian mining company Rio Tinto apologized it lost a radioactive capsule containing Caesium-137 in the Australian Outback. Authorities located the coin-size capsule after a week-long search that involved around 100 people along a 1,400-kilometer stretch of highway. Apparently, the capsule fell off a truck and landed on the side of the road. According to officials, due to the research area scope , locating the object was a monumental challenge. Contamination of the area was very unlikely; however, people were told to stay at least five meters away from the capsule because exposure could cause radiation burns or radiation sickness. Driving by was a relatively low risk, similar to taking an X-ray. The company uses the capsule to measure the density of iron ore feed from its mine in Australia’s remote Kimberley region. Difficult words: scope (the area that’s included), contaminatio n something impure from pollution or poison), exposure (affected by something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A radioactive capsule contained Caesium-137; it fell off a truck and landed on the side of the road in a remote Australian region. Mining company Rio Tinto uses the capsule to measure iron ore which comes from its mine in the Kimberley area. The company apologized for the accident and said that the capsule probably didn’t pollute the area. 100 people spent one week searching for the capsule, but the task was very difficult. They had to search a 1,400-kilometer-long area along the highway. Authorities warned people to stay at least five meters away from the capsule if they saw it. They could get radiation sickness or burns. Difficult words: capsule (a small container), remote (very far away), radiation (a dangerous energy from the smallest objects called atoms). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rio Tinto is a mining company. It has a mine in the Kimberley region, Australia. The company uses radioactive capsules to measure iron ore . A radioactive capsule is a small container with radioactive material. One capsule falls off a truck. It falls on the side of a road. 100 people look for it. Officials ask people not to get too close to the capsule. It can make them very sick or even die. People find the capsule after one week. The task is very difficult. The place is very large. The capsule is as small as a coin. Officials now say that the area is safe. Difficult words: mine (a place where workers get materials from underground), radioactive (strong and dangerous energy which comes from the smallest things called atoms), iron ore (a rock that makes hard grey metal called iron). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In June 2022, Katya Echazarreta became the first Mexican woman to travel to space when she joined the fifth crew launch of Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin. Aged 26, she also became the youngest American to visit space. Echazarreta was born in the city of Guadalajara, and she moved to the US as a child. She became a role model for people at home in Mexico. However, she was sad to talk to engineers who studied the same degree as her, but their work was to fix mobile phones or wash machines, or they gave up engineering to become paramedics or drivers. Now, Echazarreta put her career at NASA on pause to work on a bill in Mexico to boost the local aerospace industry . She says Mexico has no legal reference to regulate private companies such as SpaceX or Blue Origin to launch their rockets. Companies can’t launch their rockets in Mexico currently. Difficult words: role model (someone who others believe is a good example), aerospace industry (companies which develop and make aircrafts or satellites that fly in space), regulate (to control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Katya Echazarreta was born in Mexico, and she moved to the United States when she was a child. Recently, she became Mexico’s first astronaut when she took part in the fifth Blue Origin mission. When she was 26, she also became the youngest American to travel to space. For many Mexican people, Echazarreta became a role model . She studied engineering and became very successful. Then she saw that many engineers in Mexico became drivers or repairmen. Echazarreta decided to take a break at NASA to change laws in Mexico. At the moment, the country has no laws on the aerospace industry . For example, private companies can’t launch their rockets in Mexico. She wants to change the situation and boost the local aerospace industry. Difficult words: role model (someone who many people respect), aerospace industry (companies which make rockets and satellites and send them to space), boost (to improve). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Katya Echazarreta is born in Mexico. She moves to the United States as a child. She becomes an astronaut. Katya is Mexico’s first woman astronaut. She becomes the youngest American to go to space. She works in the Blue Origin project to travel to space. Many people love Katya. She becomes very successful. Sadly, she sees Katya that engineers in Mexico are not as lucky as her. They often become drivers or repairmen. They cannot find a job in engineering . Katya returns to Mexico. She wants to change the laws. At the moment, Mexico has no law on the aerospace industry . Companies cannot fly their rockets in Mexico. She wants to change the situation. Then many people can have a job in the aerospace industry. Difficult words: engineer (a person who makes machines and other structures), engineering (the work to make machines and other structures), aerospace industry (companies which make rockets and satellites to go to space). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1986, Christopher Knight walked into the woods in Maine. He stayed there for almost three decades as a hermit , living nearly without human contact and stealing from nearby camps. To survive the brutal winters, he built a large camp about 20 miles north of Augusta. He covered his tent with a tarp and surrounded it by camouflage garbage cans to conceal that he was there. Christopher said that the last major event he remembered happening was the Chernobyl accident in 1986, but that was not necessarily why he went into the woods. Police caught and arrested him at the Pine Tree Camp where he had been stealing food. Christopher told police officers that he had talked to only one person during all of that solitude . Police charged him with one count of burglary so far, and additional counts will likely follow during the 27 years in the woods. Difficult words: hermit (a person living alone), tarp (a strong, heavy cloth that some tents are made of), camouflage (masking), conceal (hide), solitude (loneliness), charge (officially say that somebody is guilty of a crime). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

One man from the USA lived in the woods alone for thirty years. He moved into the woods soon after the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear accident. This person has lived nearly without any human contact. He supported himself by stealing from nearby camps. Now, he has been caught and arrested . To survive the brutal winters in the woods, the man built himself a large camp. There’s no known reason for his lonely life. Difficult words: nearby (near), arrested (taken to a police station). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One man from the USA lived alone for a long time. He lived for 30 years in the woods . The man started to live in the woods soon after the Chernobyl accident. This person lived without a contact with people. He stole things from camps. People caught him when he was stealing. He is at the police station now. The winters are very hard in the woods. The man lived in a camp which he built in the woods. We don’t know why he lived alone. Difficult words: woods (forest), caught (past form of “catch”). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After she was wrongfully reported to police, Yale University honored a nine-year-old girl. Bobbi Wilson was collecting spotted lanternflies, an invasive pest , in her hometown of Caldwell, New Jersey, United States. A neighbor reported the girl to the police and claimed he was scared. After the officers spoke to the girl’s mother, they were unsure why they were there. The incident gained national attention after Bobbi’s family spoke about the dangers of racial profiling at a local council meeting. Police invited the girl to meet officers at the local police station. When she earned Yale honors, she donated her collection of lanternflies to Yale’s Peabody Museum. Difficult words: invasive (spread quickly or harmfully), pest (a destructive insect), racial profiling (think that people of a particular race behave in a certain way, or they will commit an offense). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A nine-year-old Bobbi Wilson was catching lanternflies in front of her house in New Jersey, United States. She was catching them because lanternflies were dangerous insects, and she wanted to help the environment. Suddenly, the police came and they asked the girl what she was doing. The girl’s mother was surprised why. The officers said that a neighbor called them because he was scared. The family spoke about the incident at a local council meeting. They said that the neighbor called the police only because the girl was black. People are shocked. Police officers invited Bobbi to the local police station and Yale University honored the girl. She gave her collection of lanternflies to a museum in Yale. Difficult words: lanternfly (a large insects which destroys fruit crops and trees), council (a group of people who manage a city), honor (to show respect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bobbi Wilson is nine years old. She lives in New Jersey, United States. One day, she catches dangerous insects in front of her house. Suddenly, the police come. The officers ask the girl what she is doing. The girl and her mother are surprised. They do not understand why the police come. The officers explain that a neighbor calls them. He is scared. Bobbi’s sister and mother go to a council meeting. They speak to people. They say that the man calls the police because Bobbi is black. The officers invited the girl to the police station. Yale University honors the girl for her project on insects. Bobbi gives her collection of insects to a museum in Yale University. It is a famous school. Difficult words: insects (a small animal with six legs and wings), council (a group of people who manage a city), honor (to show respect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A slimming pill killed at least 33 people in the UK; it was recently added to the country’s list of regulated poisons. DNP, or 2,4-Dinitrophenol, is classified as an explosive and banned for human consumption; however, people marketed it on the Internet as a weight-loss aid. Experts warn that DNP isn’t a medication, a recreational drug , or a nutritional supplement. It’s a toxic chemical that’s extremely dangerous at all doses, and it often leads to death. Under the Poisons Act 1973, the toxin will be regulated after October 1, 2023, so anyone who wishes to buy it will require a license from a registered pharmacist. The change follows a long campaign by the families of those who died. They hope that new restrictions ban DNP completely. Difficult words: recreational drug (a chemical substance that people take for enjoyment rather than for medical reasons), toxin (a poisonous substance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At least 33 people died in the UK after they consumed a pill to lose weight called DNP. Experts warn that DNP is a dangerous chemical, and people should never eat it. Now, officials added the chemical to the list of poisons , and from October, people will only be able to buy the drug with a license from a pharmacist. Currently, people can still buy DNP online, but experts tell them not to do it. DNP isn’t a medication or a nutritional supplement . Even a very small amount of the chemical can cause death. People died after taking DNP; their families won a long battle with authorities to change the chemical’s classification . Still the families say that we must ban DNP quickly so that nobody else dies. Difficult words: poison (a substance which can make someone sick or even kill him), nutritional supplement (a product which people eat, and it contains vitamins or minerals), cla ssification (an official name or type for a thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least 33 people die in the UK. They use a slimming pill. A slimming pill helps people lose weight. This slimming pill is called DNP. It is very dangerous. Toxic things are in the pill. It can kill a person. People should never use DNP. Last week, British authorities say that DNP is a poison . Sadly, people can still buy it on the Internet. In October, people can only buy it with a special document from a pharmacist . People die and their families want to help. They say that authorities must ban the pill quickly. More people can die. Difficult words: poison (a dangerous substance which can make you sick or kill you), pharmacist (a person who prepares and sells drugs and medicines), ban (to make something impossible officially). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After days of increasing pressure, Germany decided to send 14 Leopard II tanks to Ukraine. They will also allow other countries to send their German tanks. The action is the first time since World War II that German battle tanks have appeared on a European battlefield. This fact may not change the war’s end, but it definitely changes the political scenario . Germany’s announcement leads the way for other Western countries to supply help to Ukraine. Finland, Spain, Poland, Estonia, Norway, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom are also considering sending tanks to fight. For months, Ukraine has been asking Western countries for more modern battle tanks to increase mobility and firepower; however, only time will tell if this united Western effort will help Ukraine push back Russia’s invasion forces. Russia’s ambassador in Washington warned that any deliveries of US tanks would be an open provocation , and the Kremlin said that this decision would have terrible consequences for the West. Difficult words: scenario (a development of events), provocation (an action or speech that makes someone angry). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For several months, Ukraine asked western countries for help to fight Russia. Ukraine asked for more modern tanks , but some countries were afraid to openly help Ukraine. Last week, Germany decided to send 14 modern tanks to Ukraine. Other countries will send their German tanks, too. This event will be the first time since World War II that German tanks will fight in Europe. Other countries including Finland, Poland, and the United Kingdom are also thinking they may send tanks to Ukraine. Russian officials said that if they do it, they will have a terrible impact on Europe. Russia’s ambassador in United States said that if the US sent tanks to Russia, it would be an open provocation . Difficult words: tank (a very heavy vehicle to fight), ambassador (a person who lives in a foreign country and he represents his own), provocation (words or actions to make somebody else angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For several months, Ukraine asks Western countries for help. Ukraine needs modern tanks to fight against Russia. Last week, Germany says that it will send 14 tanks to Ukraine. Other countries have German tanks. They can send them to Ukraine, too. German tanks do not fight anywhere in Europe since World War II. Other European countries want to send help to Ukraine. These countries are for example Finland, Poland, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Russian officials say that they will destroy Western tanks. If the United States send tanks, too, it will make Russia very angry. Difficult words: tank (a very heavy vehicle to fight), destroy (to damage something so badly that you cannot use it anymore). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Apple’s anticipated mixed-reality headset is an ambitious attempt at a 3D version of the iPhone’s operating system. It has eye and hand-tracking systems that could set the technology ahead of rival products. The roughly 3,000-dollar device is due later this year under the likely name of Reality Pro, and it’ll take a novel approach to virtual meetings and immersive video. It wants to change a VR industry that Meta currently dominates. Apple is expanding into its first major new product category since it released its smartwatch in 2015. The company is entering an uncertain market with an expensive product, and it needs to wow customers. Apple’s 1,000-person-plus Technology Development Group has spent more than seven years on this project, and the company is counting on it as a new revenue source. Difficult words: novel (new and different), immersive (complete involvement in a particular activity), wow (to impress). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Company Apple last introduced a new product in 2015 when it introduced its smartwatch. Now, Apple seems ready to introduce something very different. The new product is a mixed-reality headset, and users will control it by eye and hand. Users will hold virtual meetings and play 3D videos. Currently, company Meta dominates the VR market, and Apple hopes that its product will bring a different experience than its rival . Apple’s team of a thousand people worked on the product for more than seven years, and it hopes to impress customers. The headset should be on sale later this year, and its price will be about 3,000 dollars. Difficult words: dominate (to control something), VR (virtual reality), rival (a person or thing that competes in the same activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Company Apple works on a new product. The product is a mixed-reality headset . It mixes real and digital realities. Users will control the device by hand and eye. The technology is very new. You can have virtual meetings and watch 3D videos. Only company Meta has a similar product. Apple’s product must be very special. The last product from Apple is its smartwatch. The company first sells it in 2015. Apple has a team of 1,000 people. They work for seven years on the headset. Apple hopes that the headset will bring it a lot of money. Difficult words: mixed-reality (put more than one experience together), headset (a device which a person wears on his head, and it connects to a phone or computer), virtual (something that is in a computer but not in the real world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Friday, on the annual International Holocaust Remembrance Day, the United Nations held its annual memorial service to honor the victims and survivors of the Holocaust. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres warned that neo-Nazi white supremacist movements were more dangerous, and they represented the number one internal security threat for several countries. Surveys show that anti-Semitism is at record highs, including racism, prejudice against Muslims, homophobia, and misogyny . The UN General Assembly designated January 27 as International Holocaust Remembrance day; on this day in 1945, the Soviet Army liberated Auschwitz, an infamous Nazi concentration camp in German-occupied Poland. On this day, the UN urges all member states to honor the six million of victims of Nazism and to develop educational programs to prevent future genocides . Difficult words: supremacist (beliefs that a particular type or group of people are better than others), misogyny (dislike or prejudice against women), genocide (murder of certain people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On January 27, 1945, the Soviet Army freed a concentration camp in Auschwitz, Poland. The United Nations chose this day as the International Holocaust Remembrance Day. On this day, the world remembers people who died during or survived the Holocaust. Six million Jewish people died, and millions of others were victims of Nazism during this time. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres warned of dangerous groups of people who support neo-Nazism and anti-Semitism , as they believe that white people were better than others. Guterres also said that these groups of people were very dangerous, and in several countries, they were a risk to overall security. Difficult words: concentration camp (a place where large numbers of people stay and work, and many of them are killed there), victims (a person who is hurt or killed), neo-Nazism (ideas that support Germany’s Nazism), anti-Semitism (a strong dislike of Jewish people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

January 27 is the International Holocaust Remembrance Day. The world remembers people who die in or survive the Holocaust. The Holocaust is the name for the terrible things that Nazi Germany does in World War II. Nazis kill six million Jewish people and millions of other people. Many people die in concentration camps . Hundreds of camps are in Nazi Germany. The largest concentration camp for Jews is in Auschwitz, Poland. Soviet soldiers liberate it on January 27, 1945. Last Friday, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres speaks to world leaders. He says that people must remember what happens during World War II. In some countries, groups of people believe that Nazism is good. They believe that white people are better than others. This idea is very dangerous. Difficult words: concentration camp (a place where very many people live and work, especially during World War II), liberate (to set free), Nazism (political ideas of Germany between 1933 and 1945). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Doomsday Clock is an idea that scientists use to show how close they think we are to nuclear destruction of the planet. In 1947, Albert Einstein and other the scientists created the clock. When it first started ticking, it sat at seven minutes to midnight. However, two years later, the Soviet Union tested its first atomic bomb, and the hand moved to three minutes to midnight. In 1991, as the Cold War cooled down, the clock was set at its furthest time from catastrophe of 17 minutes to midnight. In the years since, the clock’s hand creeped closer to midnight, and thanks to geopolitical tensions and the climate crisis, it got to 100 seconds to midnight. Each year, nuclear technology and climate science experts discuss world events and where to move the clock’s hand. The closer they place it to midnight, the closer they think we are to annihilation . Last week, they reset the clock to 90 seconds to midnight, so the world is closer to ending than ever before. Difficult words: geopolitical (political activity influenced by the physical features of a country or area), annihilation (complete destruction). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 1947, a group of scientists including Albert Einstein created the so-called Doomsday Clock. Every year, nuclear and climate experts meet and move the clock’s hand. If the scientists think that the world is getting closer to a catastrophe , they move its hand closer to midnight. When the clock first started ticking, its hand was seven minutes before midnight. When the Soviet Union tested the first atomic bomb in 1949, scientists moved the clock’s hand to three minutes to midnight. In 1991, the hand moved down to 17 minutes to midnight, the farthest it ever was. Since that time, the hand moved closer and closer to midnight because of the climate crisis and geopolitical problems. Last week, scientists moved the clock’s hand to 90 seconds to midnight. We are closer to destroying the planet than ever before. Difficult words: catastrophe (a sudden tragic event), climate crisis (dangerous changes of the world’s weather and the impact of these changes), geopolitical (the politics of a country or area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1947, a group of scientists create the Doomsday Clock. One of the scientists is the famous Albert Einstein. The clock is not an actual clock. It is an idea. Every year, nuclear and climate experts meet. They speak about the situation in the world. They decide if people are bringing the world to its end. They move the clock’s hand. If they think that the world is closer to its end, they move the hand closer to midnight. When the clock starts, the hand is seven minutes to midnight. The hand moves three minutes from midnight during the Cold War . Last week, experts move the hand to 90 seconds to midnight. The move is the closest ever. Scientists think that the world is very close to a terrible event. Difficult words: nuclear (related to the smallest things called atoms), climate (the world’s weather), Cold War (the war without fights between the US and Russia). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Following the collapse of the Zimbabwean dollar in 2009, Zimbabwe became a dual currency economy. The government reintroduced Zimbabwean dollars in 2019; however, the local people generally rely on the US dollar for daily transactions. With US currency in short supply, well-worn bills are popular. Some people buy old bills at a discount; shops would usually reject the bills. The people fix the notes and sell them for a profit on the black market. Zimbabwean banks have mandates to accept soiled money in exchange for crisp notes. The government bank has asked citizens to make exchanges; however, many people mistrust the financial system because they lost their savings due to hyperinflation . They prefer black market traders. Difficult words: dual (consisting of two parts), crisp (clear and hard), hyperinflation (out-of-control general price increases in an economy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Zimbabwe uses two currencies : the US dollar and the Zimbabwean dollar. The government reintroduced the Zimbabwean dollar in 2019, but many people prefer to use the US dollar. US dollars aren’t easy to find, but people found a solution. They buy old and torn notes which they can’t use in shops. They fix the notes and sell them on the black market . Officials say that people should take these notes to banks because they must accept them and change them for new notes. Many people don’t believe the banks. They lost all their money because of the government’s financial problems, and they prefer to sell their money on the black market. Difficult words: currency (the money of a country), torn (to pull someone in two parts), black market (illegally buy and sell things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Zimbabwe has two types of money. One is the US dollar. The other is the Zimbabwean dollar. Since 2019, people use the Zimbabwean dollar again. They like the US dollar better. The country doesn’t have enough US notes . People fix this problem. People fix old notes. Some of them are torn. Torn is when they are in several parts. People should take them to a bank. Banks must change these notes for new ones. People sell money on the black market . They do not believe the banks anymore. The banks lose their savings. High inflation makes them lose money. Difficult words: note (a piece of paper money), black market (buy and sell things which are against the law), inflation (when prices grow and people buy less). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of children in China have a dangerous journey to get home from school because they have to climb over a mountain cliff using wooden ladders. To reach their remote village, they climb about twenty metres to the top while carrying bags or other items. Villagers and even dogs travel this way, making it look almost easy. However, it is terrifying for some people, as they say it makes their legs shiver and they dare not look down. Getting to the top is a relief as family and friends greet these children. Many of the students study in a school thirty miles away and have not been home in months. The people in the village long for a safer way to get there, but they believe that a better future lies in getting education for their children. Difficult words: shiver (shake), dare (be brave and do something), long for (want to have). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A group of children from one village in China face a dangerous journey home from school. If they want to get home, the children have to climb over a big mountain. The children climb about twenty metres on the ladders to the top of the mountain. They carry their bags and other things, too. A dog also uses the ladders. Parents are always very happy when they see their children again. The parents want a better way to get into their village. They also believe that a better future lies in their children’s education. Difficult words: face (deal with), ladder (thing for climbing made of wood or metal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of Chinese children from one village have a dangerous way home from school. If they want to go home, they must go over a big mountain. The children go only up and up twenty meters. It is very dangerous. When they go up, they have to carry their bags and other things, too. One dog uses this way, also. The parents are always very happy when they see their children again. The parents want a better way to their village. They also believe that school is very important for their children. Difficult words: dangerous (not safe), important (needed for life). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A four year old chihuahua named Honey may be small, but she makes up for it in courage. She showed this skill off after a much bigger pit bull attacked her owner’s granddaughter, Jenna. Honey came to her rescue, bravely drawing the aggressive dog away. People later caught the pit bull and put it down . The pit bull had bit Jenna so badly that she needed over a hundred stitches to fix her eye and hours of surgery. It could have been much worse, however, if the brave chihuahua had not sprung into action. Difficult words: make up for (compensate), put down (kill), stitch (a special thing for closing a cut), sprung (moved quickly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The chihuahua is a small type of dog. It may be small but it can be very brave. One chihuahua helped a small girl when she was attacked by a pit bull. The chihuahua came to help the girl and managed to get the aggressive dog away from her. People caught the pit bull and they will kill it. The girl has terrible injuries and she will need hours of surgery . But if the chihuahua had not helped her, it could have been much worse. Difficult words: injury (broken or cut part of your body), surgery (operation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section

The chihuahua is a small dog. It is small but it can be very brave . One chihuahua helped a small girl when she was attacked by a pit bull. The chihuahua came to help the girl and was able to get the bad dog away from the girl. People have the bad dog now. They will kill the dog. The girl has big problems with her face. She will need hours of operations. But without the chihuahua’s help, the girl would have bigger problems. Difficult words: brave (when you are brave, you have no fear), attack (be aggressive and hit somebody). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In November 2008, Dubai’s first Atlantis hotel opened with a 5-million-dollar firework display, A-list guests from around the world, and a performance by pop star Kylie Minogue. 14 years later, another Atlantis hotel named Atlantis the Royal opened just a short stroll away from the original resort. Last weekend, it opened with the same extravagance . Beyonce performed to a VIP audience for 24 million dollars, and fireworks lit up the sky above the city’s famous artificial island of Palm Jumeirah. The hotel has nearly 800 rooms and it’ll open to paying customers on February 10, 2023. It has seven bars and restaurants, 90 pools, gyms, spas, and many other amenities to bring in wealthy vacationers. The daily rate ranges from 1,000 dollars a night to 100,000 for the most luxurious suite. Difficult words: A-list (a group of the most successful and famous people and organizations), extravagance (spend more money than is necessary or reasonable), amenity (something that provides comfort and enjoyment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2008, Dubai’s first Atlantis hotel opened with fireworks which cost 5 million dollars. Singer Kylie Minogue performed at the party for the most famous people in the world. Two months later, Dubai started to have money problems, but now, a second Atlantis hotel is opening. It is called Atlantis the Royal. Singer Beyonce performed for a reported 24 million dollars, and she gave her first performance since 2020. Fireworks lit the sky above the island of Palm Jumeirah. The hotel will open on February 10, 2023, with nearly 800 rooms, seven bars and restaurants, 90 pools, gyms, and spas . One night at Atlantis The Royal will cost from 1,000 to 100,000 dollars. Difficult words: performance (when a singer or actor plays or sings in front of people), spa (a place where people can take a bath, get a massage, or go in a sauna). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Atlantis hotels are famous and nice hotels. In 2008, the first Atlantis hotel opens in Dubai. A big party happens. Singer Kylie Minogue sings in front of many famous people. Fireworks for the party cost 5 million dollars. Last week, a second Atlantis hotel opens in Dubai. It is called Atlantis the Royal. Beyonce sings at the event. Reports say that she gets 24 million dollars for her performance . Palm Jumeirah is an island. It looks like a palm tree. Big fireworks are above the island. The hotel has nearly 800 rooms. Seven bars and restaurants are in the hotel. Guests can go to many gyms and spas . One night at the hotel costs from 1,000 to 100,000 dollars. Difficult words: fireworks (bright colored displays in the sky), performance (when a person sings or plays in front of other people), spa (a place where people can take a bath get a massage, or go in a sauna). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Burkina Faso decided to end a military agreement with France; it allowed French troops to fight militants on its territory. The West African country is facing insurgency by Al-Qaeda and Islamic State groups; they have taken over large swathes of land and displaced millions of people. On January 18, 2023, the government suspended the 2018 military government with Paris, and it gave France one month to withdraw its troops. The government spokesman Emmanuel Rodrigo said that the vision of Burkina Faso’s transitional government was to defend itself; however, it diplomatic relations with France would continue, and Burkina Faso still wanted support for military equipment. French influence has been declining in its former colonies. Military groups lead Burkina Faso and neighboring Mali. The groups seized power in the past two years, and they burned bridges with their traditional allies. Difficult words: insurgency (a violent act or plan by a group of people who refuse to accept their government’s power), transitional government (a temporary government that governs until official elections take place in a country), burn bridges (to permanently end relations with another person or organization). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, Burkina Faso announced that it would end a 2018 deal with France, and all French soldiers had to leave the country. Burkina Faso has big problems with militant groups who control large parts of the country. Millions of people left their homes because of violent conflicts. The spokesman of Burkina Faso’s government said that the country needed to defend itself, but it would still need guns from France. France is losing power in its former colonies , such as Burkina Faso or Mali. Last year, French soldiers left Mali, and the country hired Russian soldiers to fight the militants. The French president replied that Russia wanted power in troubled African countries. Difficult words: militant group (a group of people who fight against the government), defend (to keep safe from attack or harm), colony (a country or area which is under the control of another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2018, France and Burkina Faso make a deal. French soldiers help fight against militants in Burkina Faso. Currently, the situation in Burkina Faso is dangerous. Militants control large parts of the country. Many conflicts happen. Millions of people leave their homes. Burkina Faso doesn’t want help from France anymore. Officials there say that the country must solve its own problems. French soldiers must leave soon. Still, Burkina Faso wants guns from France. Last year, French soldiers leave Mali. Mali and Burkina Faso are French colonies . France is losing control of its colonies. Russian soldiers help in Mali now. People do not know if Russian soldiers will help in Burkina Faso, too. Difficult words: militant (a person who fights against a government), conflict (a fight), colony (a country or place which another country controls). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After a series of children deaths linked to cough syrups, the World Health Organization (WHO) called for immediate action against contaminated medicines. Last year, more than 300 children, mostly younger than five years, in Gambia, Indonesia, and Uzbekistan died of acute kidney injuries. Authorities linked these deaths to over-the-counter cough syrups with high levels of chemicals. These chemicals can be fatal in small amounts, and thus, they should never be in medicines. According to the WHO, the news impacts the Philippines, Senegal, and Cambodia because they have these medicines in their stores. The WHO called for action across its 194 member states to prevent more deaths. The involved companies denied their products were contaminated. However, the WHO called for more oversight from governments and regulators and for drug manufacturers to test their products thoroughly with records of the process. Difficult words: over-the-counter (sold legally without a prescription from a doctor), fatal (cause death), oversight (watchful and responsible care). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than 300 children died in Gambia, Indonesia, and Uzbekistan after they used cough syrups. The syrups had dangerous chemicals which caused serious kidney problems. These chemicals were so dangerous that small amounts were deadly, and they should not be in any medicines. People bought the syrups without prescriptions from a doctor. The WHO said that the syrups were on sale in the Philippines, Senegal, and Cambodia, too. The WHO asked all 194 member groups to take action. Governments and regulators need to watch drug manufacturers to confirm that they test their medicines well. Difficult words: on sale (available for people to buy), prescription (a piece of paper which a doctor writes and gives you the right to get a medicine at a drugstore), regulator (an organization which controls the activities of businesses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 300 children die in Gambia, Indonesia, and Uzbekistan. The children use a cough syrup. The medicine usually helps with a cough or a cold. Dangerous chemicals are in the syrups. The chemicals make the children have serious kidney problems. Little amounts of the chemical are deadly. These chemicals must not be in the syrups. People buy the syrup in stores. They do not need their doctor to help them buy it. The World Health Organization says that people can buy the syrups in the Philippines, Senegal, and Cambodia. Authorities must check companies carefully that make medicines. Companies must test their products more often. Difficult words: chemical (a thing that is sometimes in certain products), kidney (one of the two body parts which take away water and some chemicals from the blood), amount (a number of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On the 50th anniversary of the now-overturned Roe vs. Wade ruling, anti-abortion demonstrators lined the streets of Washington DC, United States. The rally is called the March for Life and has happened every year since 1973. This rally was the first since June 2022 when the US Supreme Court overturned the important legislation. It had made access to abortion a federal right in the US. However, since its repeal , abortion is no longer protected under federal law, so individual states change access to abortion. Pro-life supporters want to completely ban abortions. The issue is contentious in US politics, and President Biden pledged to try to restore abortion rights, but he cannot do a lot. Difficult words: repeal (to cancel a law), pro-life (the idea that a pregnant woman shouldn’t have the freedom to choose an abortion), contentious (cause disagreement and argument). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In June 2022, the US Supreme Court canceled the US federal law which gave pregnant women the right to decide if they wanted an abortion . Since that time, each US state has its own laws about abortion. This topic causes many arguments, and the US president wants to change the law again. He believes that women should be free to decide if they want to have a child. He doesn’t have enough support to make any changes in the law. Last week, the March of Life took place in Washington DC. It is an anti-abortion protest which happens every year since 1973. Protesters want to make abortion completely illegal in the US. Difficult words: federal (the country’s government and not a local government), abortion (a surgery which ends a pregnancy), anti-abortion (the idea that abortion is wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the past, pregnant women have a choice in the US. They can decide if they want to have the baby. A law says they can decide. The situation changes in June 2022. A court cancels this law. Now, every US state has its own rules. Abortion is against the law in some states. Many people protest . The US president wants to change the law. He believes that every woman can decide if she wants a baby. The president does not have enough power to change the law. A protest happens in Washington DC. It happens every year since 1973. Protesters say that abortion should be against the law in the county. Difficult words: pregnant (a woman who has a baby inside her body), abortion (a surgery which means that a woman is not pregnant anymore), protest (to say or show you are not happy with the government; a protester is a person who protests). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
